svg.title: For q = 0 both moduli equal one. Equivalently, scalar multiplication by λ−1 has operator norm at most one on the coefficient space. Thus the first smallness expression is 1/x ≤1, and the second is |λ−1|/4 ≤1/4. A lower bound on the norm of a general operator would not imply this inverse bound; the scalar identity is what proves it here. The target march allowances satisfy Wv ≤δmI′ v, so their products meet the insertion substitution bound. Applying the local fusion estimate yields a coefficient Q0 with ∥Q0∥coeff≤p′ = aq m+1x 4/z
